description: Case 05 — verifier evaluating two candidate findings of different types: a deterministic invalid_code (captured value 9 not in allowed codes) and an LLM-based insufficient_probing (2-word answer after PROBE FULLY instruction). Both confirmed. Illustrates the verifier reasoning about evidence from different detection pathways.

verified_findings.claim: Captured value is not a valid questionnaire code
verified_findings.verifier_reason: The captured value 9 is not among the allowed codes 1, 2, or 3 defined for Q1.

verified_findings.claim: The open-ended response may not have been probed sufficiently

evidence.expected_question: Why did production change? PROBE FULLY

verified_findings.verifier_reason: The expected instruction was 'PROBE FULLY' but the spoken answer is only two words ('Demand grew'), indicating insufficient probing of the open-ended response.
verified_findings.detection_pathway: LLM — semantic judgment of probing sufficiency

verifier_note: Neither finding was rejected in the recorded runs. The verifier confirmed both using separate reasoning chains. For the deterministic finding (invalid_code) the verifier simply validated the code-lookup result; for the LLM finding (insufficient_probing) it evaluated the answer length and missing probe instruction against questionnaire requirements. The insufficient_probing finding is a false positive in this case (not in ground_truth). No rejections appear in the five sampled trajectories — this is consistent with the recall-biased detector design (FP=16 in the main eval run).
